Maintenance is part of the design

A feature is not complete when its happy path works. Operators also need to know how evidence ages, which failures are retried, and what must happen before an old binary can be restored.

A system's interface includes the facts a caller and an operator must know to use it correctly, not only the names and types accepted by a function.

That observation changes where cleanup belongs. Retention is coupled to recovery guarantees, so its lower bound should be validated next to the timing settings that define those guarantees.

It also changes testing. A test that injects failure before and after the durable effect demonstrates ownership more convincingly than a diagram that merely labels a transaction module.
